jlbind

Call Julia code from R without starting a Julia session.

jlbind compiles Julia code into a shared library with JuliaC.jl (by default with --trim=safe), and R calls it through R’s official C API. Thus, there is almost no overhead (see Performance).

Several R packages using jlbind can be installed side by side: their Julia code is compiled into one shared library.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("BjarkeHautop/jlbind")

Building the shared library requires Julia >= 1.13. Installing jlbind does not itself build the library.

Using a package built on jlbind

After installing or updating an R package that uses jlbind, build the shared library:

jlbind::install_backend()

This compiles the Julia code of every installed package that uses jlbind and may take a few minutes. Run it again whenever you install or update one of them.

Writing a package that uses jlbind

Set up a package with jlbind::use_jlbind(), then declare the Julia functions R can call in the generated binding package under inst/julia/:

module MyPkgBindings

using JLBind

greet(name::String) = "Hello, " * name * "!"
@rcall greet(name::String)::String

end

Run jlbind::update_entrypoints(), and call the function from R:

greet <- function(name) .Call(C_greet, name)

See Writing a package that uses jlbind for a full walkthrough.
